children: CEO Mark Zuckerberg has pushed back against calls for a coordinated slowdown in AI development, saying AI labs should decide individually how to manage the risks from increasingly capable systems.
Zuckerberg said AI labs have both the responsibility and incentive to build safely, putting him broadly in line with Nvidia
CEO Jensen Huang, who has also pushed back against efforts to coordinate a slowdown in AI development.
“Engaging independent evaluators and advisors is industry best practice,” Zuckerberg wrote in a post on X.com. He cited Meta’s
decision to delay its Muse AI launch for several months over safety and security concerns.
“We didn’t call for everyone else to do this before we would. We just did it as part of our day-to-day work because it was clearly the right thing for people and for us.” he said.

Zuckerberg said there is a growing debate over slowing AI development until alignment catches up but argued that “trust and alignment are quickly becoming the most important capabilities that will differentiate agents and models.”
He also said AI labs have strong incentives to prevent their models from causing harm because they face “significant liability if their models cause harm.”
CEO Dario Amodei has called for greater coordination among AI companies as models become more capable. Nvidia’s
Huang has separately pushed back against calls for a coordinated slowdown in AI development.

title: Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg joins Nvidia’s Huang in pushing back against AI slowdown
